<section id="Ax1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix">Appendix Table of Contents</h2>

<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Limitations</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Reported times and costs reflect API inference conditions at the time of
evaluation (Appendix <a href="#A10" title="Appendix J Experimental Details ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">J</span></a>). Providers control
subsequent changes to inference speed and pricing. We validate representative
task subsets on held-out agents (Appendix <a href="#A7" title="Appendix G Representative Task Selection ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">G</span></a>); subset scores
approximate full-benchmark performance. Changes in agent capabilities may
require revalidation of these subsets.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Our evaluations cover a broad range of agents across four benchmarks
(Appendix <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Full Evaluation Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a>). Evaluation cost limits coverage of every
combination of model, harness, reasoning effort, and benchmark.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Infrastructure: Technical Details</h2>

<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Agent and Environment Sandboxes</h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We run the agent and task environment in separate sandboxes. The
environment contains the desktop, applications, and initial task state;
the agent interacts with it through screenshot and action requests.
Task initialization and verification remain independent of the agent,
allowing the same agent implementation to run across benchmarks.
When the agent terminates or reaches its limit, the benchmark’s verifier
scores the trajectory or final environment state.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We use Modal to host the sandboxes and adapt the environment runtime
from Gym-Anything <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Aggarwal et al., 2026</a>)</cite>.
The environment measures task time and the time spent executing actions
and returning observations, independently of the agent implementation.
As in Sec. <a href="#S2.SS1" title="2.1 Standardized Computer-Use Evaluation ‣ 2 Method ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a>, task preparation, agent
initialization, and verification are excluded from task time.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Model Serving, Resource Allocation, and Parallel Evaluation</h3>

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Agents access models through API endpoints or a self-hosted vLLM
inference server <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kwon et al., 2023</a>)</cite>.
We use L40S GPUs for self-hosted inference.
The evaluation configuration specifies the compute resources, task
limits, and number of concurrent agents. Model initialization and
weight loading finish before task timing begins.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We assign tasks to available agents and environments. Each task starts
from a fresh environment state. Its clock starts after the agent and
environment are ready and stops when the agent finishes or reaches its
limit, excluding time waiting for an execution slot. Model servers reuse
loaded weights across tasks. We record a trajectory for each task.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.3 </span>Fast I/O Implementation</h3>

<div id="A2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">FastCUA, our Fast I/O implementation, reduces the time between issuing
an action and receiving a screenshot. We encode screenshots in the
background and combine action execution and screenshot delivery in a
single request.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Screenshot capture and encoding.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use QEMU’s D-Bus display interface to keep the current screen in memory
and encode updated frames in the background.
We use JPEG at quality 95 with no chroma subsampling and retain the
full <math id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1920\times 1080" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1920</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1080</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1920\times 1080</annotation></semantics></math> resolution.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Action execution and communication.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We execute the action and return its screenshot in one request, reusing
the network connection across requests. A lightweight command client
reduces per-action startup overhead. We also place
agent and environment sandboxes in the same Modal region to reduce
network latency. Fast I/O returns the screenshot as soon as action
execution and image preparation finish.
It can therefore return a screenshot before the application has updated
its interface, as illustrated in Figure <a href="#S3.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ The Pareto frontier changes across benchmarks. ‣ 3.2 Analysis ‣ 3 Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.4 </span>Action Latency: Fast I/O, Gym-Anything, and OSWorld</h3>

<figure id="A2.T1" class="ltx_table">
<table id="A2.T1.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">

<tr id="A2.T1.2.2" class="ltx_tr">

<td id="A2.T1.2.4.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_bb"><span id="A2.T1.2.4.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">14.98</span></td></tr>

</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 1: </span><span id="A2.T1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Fast I/O reduces action-to-observation latency to milliseconds.</span>
Median latency in milliseconds over 20 calls per action. For each system,
the timer starts immediately before <span id="A2.T1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">env.step(action)</span> and stops
when it returns the observation. All default action waits are included.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Fast I/O reduces latency by one to three orders of magnitude.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A2.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ B.4 Action Latency: Fast I/O, Gym-Anything, and OSWorld ‣ Appendix B Infrastructure: Technical Details ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> compares Fast I/O with
Gym-Anything <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Aggarwal et al., 2026</a>)</cite> and
OSWorld <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xie et al., 2024</a>)</cite> for mouse
clicks, key presses, and text entry.
Fast I/O takes 2.4–27.6 ms per call, compared to 2.5–3.5 s for the
existing implementations. For example, a click takes 27.6 ms compared with
2.8 s with Gym-Anything, while typing 100 characters takes 15.0 ms
compared with 3.5 s.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Measurement setup.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We time each runtime’s native <span id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">env.step(action)</span> call, from issuing
the action until the observation is returned. We test four actions on a
<math id="A2.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1920\times 1080" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1920</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1080</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1920\times 1080</annotation></semantics></math> Ubuntu desktop: clicking the Activities button, pressing
Escape, pressing Ctrl+U, and typing 100 ASCII characters into a terminal.
The caller and VM run in the same Modal sandbox. OSWorld uses its Docker
provider with screenshot observations; both
baselines use their default waits and action implementations.
Table <a href="#A2.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ B.4 Action Latency: Fast I/O, Gym-Anything, and OSWorld ‣ Appendix B Infrastructure: Technical Details ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> reports the median of 20 calls per action,
without profiling. Setup, pauses between calls, and saving returned
screenshots occur outside the timed interval.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.5 </span>Latency Breakdown</h3>

<figure id="A2.T2" class="ltx_table">
<table id="A2.T2.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="A2.T2.2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A2.T2.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt">Component (ms)</th>
<td id="A2.T2.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_tt">Click</td>
<td id="A2.T2.2.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_tt">Escape</td>
<td id="A2.T2.2.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_tt">Ctrl+U</td>
<td id="A2.T2.2.1.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_tt">Type 100 characters</td></tr>
<tr id="A2.T2.2.2" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A2.T2.2.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_t" colspan="5"><span id="A2.T2.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Gym-Anything</span></th></tr>
<tr id="A2.T2.2.3" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A2.T2.2.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row">Fixed waits</th>
<td id="A2.T2.2.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right">2100.2</td>

<section id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Where do the baselines spend time?</h5>

<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A2.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ B.5 Latency Breakdown ‣ Appendix B Infrastructure: Technical Details ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> shows that fixed sleeps account for
most of the baseline latency. Both implementations sleep for two seconds
after an action, and Gym-Anything adds another 100 ms per step.
Subtracting the two-second sleep leaves 804–1524 ms for
Gym-Anything and 524–769 ms for OSWorld. Gym-Anything captures a PNG
with FFmpeg, transfers it, and deletes the temporary file; typing also
adds a 6 ms interval between characters. In OSWorld, most of the
remaining time is spent in the action and screenshot requests, including
processing inside the VM and communication.</p>
</div>

<section id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Full command-to-screenshot latency.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A2.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ Where do the baselines spend time? ‣ B.5 Latency Breakdown ‣ Appendix B Infrastructure: Technical Details ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> measures latency from the agent issuing a
command to receiving the screenshot file, including communication
between sandboxes. We place both sandboxes in New York and test the four
actions on two OSWorld desktops, with 0.5 s and 8 s gaps between
requests. All 80 timed commands complete in under 50 ms.
Median times are 38.5 ms for a click, 12.8 ms for
Escape, 13.6 ms for Ctrl+U, and 29.5 ms for typing 100 characters.
Communication contributes 4.6–5.0 ms on average. Image preparation
after the request takes 0.02–0.27 ms; encoding runs in the background.
Clicks take longer because input execution
includes a 25 ms interval between pressing and releasing the mouse button.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.6 </span>Fast I/O Consistency Across Five Seeds</h3>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 4: </span><span id="A2.T4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Fast I/O remains consistent across five evaluations.</span>
Each row averages all 50 OSWorld tasks for GPT-6 Astra at low reasoning
effort. SD is the sample standard deviation across run-level means;
score SD is in percentage points. Steps count action batches, and
waits are explicitly requested by the agent.</figcaption>

<section id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Environment processing time remains low across runs.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A2.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ B.6 Fast I/O Consistency Across Five Seeds ‣ Appendix B Infrastructure: Technical Details ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> reports five evaluations of GPT-6 Astra
at low effort on the same 50 OSWorld tasks with Fast I/O. We keep the
agent prompt fixed and use fresh task seeds, a 500-step limit, and agent
and environment sandboxes in New York.
Environment time excluding agent-requested waits is
<math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.336\pm 0.015" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.336</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.015</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.336\pm 0.015</annotation></semantics></math> s per task (mean <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> standard deviation across runs).
The mean task time is <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="99.0\pm 3.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>99.0</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>3.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">99.0\pm 3.9</annotation></semantics></math> s, and the score is
<math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="90.4\pm 1.8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>90.4</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>1.8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">90.4\pm 1.8</annotation></semantics></math>%.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Most environment time is spent on agent-requested waits.</h5>

<div id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A2.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ B.6 Fast I/O Consistency Across Five Seeds ‣ Appendix B Infrastructure: Technical Details ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> also separates the waits requested by the
agent from other environment processing. These waits account for
<math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4.739" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4.739</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4.739</annotation></semantics></math> s of the <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.075" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5.075</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.075</annotation></semantics></math> s of mean environment time per task, leaving
only <math id="A2.SS6.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.336" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.336</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.336</annotation></semantics></math> s for the remaining processing.
Appendix <a href="#A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2" title="Agent time, environment time, and requested waits. ‣ Appendix D Interaction and Token Measurements ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a> defines these timing components.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Implementing and Evaluating an Agent</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To evaluate a new agent with <span id="A3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">cua-speedrun</span>, users implement its model
calls, prompts, and interaction history. The infrastructure handles task
setup, desktop interaction, and verification through the common interface
in Sec. <a href="#S2.SS3" title="2.3 Infrastructure ‣ 2 Method ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a>. The same agent implementation and
environment interface can then be used across benchmarks.</p>
</div>
<section id="A3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1 </span>Agent Templates</h3>

<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We provide templates for direct model-API agents, Codex, Claude Code,
and open-weight agents served through vLLM. Each template contains two
files: <span id="A3.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">init.py</span> prepares dependencies and model serving, and
<span id="A3.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">agent.py</span> implements the agent loop.
Initialization finishes before task timing begins. Users can retain
<span id="A3.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">init.py</span> and modify only the agent loop to test a new model,
prompt, or interaction strategy.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2 </span>Minimal Agent Example</h3>

<div id="A3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Listing <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_label ltx_ref_self"></span> shows a minimal agent. The script receives the
environment URL and task instruction as command-line arguments and uses
the <span id="A3.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Computer</span> client to request screenshots, execute actions,
and end the task. In each iteration, <span id="A3.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">choose_actions</span> receives
the instruction, screenshot, and interaction history. This user-defined
function calls the model and returns an action list, or <span id="A3.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">None</span>
when the agent considers the task complete. Users determine how to
present this information to the model.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<div id="A3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_listing ltx_lstlisting ltx_listing"><div class="ltx_listing_data"><a href="data:text/plain;base64," download="">⬇</a></div>
<div id="lstnumberx1" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">import</span><span id="lstnumberx1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">os</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx2" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">import</span><span id="lstnumberx2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">sys</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx3" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">from</span><span id="lstnumberx3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">cua_speedrun</span>.<span id="lstnumberx3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">client</span><span id="lstnumberx3.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx3.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">import</span><span id="lstnumberx3.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx3.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">Computer</span>

<div id="lstnumberx7" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span><span id="lstnumberx7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">history</span><span id="lstnumberx7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>=<span id="lstnumberx7.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>[]

</div>
<div id="lstnumberx9" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span><span id="lstnumberx9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">for</span><span id="lstnumberx9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx9.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">_</span><span id="lstnumberx9.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx9.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">in</span><span id="lstnumberx9.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx9.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">range</span>(<span id="lstnumberx9.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">limit</span>):

<div id="lstnumberx10" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span><span id="lstnumberx10.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">observation</span><span id="lstnumberx10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>=<span id="lstnumberx10.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx10.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">computer</span>.<span id="lstnumberx10.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">observe</span>()

<div id="lstnumberx12" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx12.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span><span id="lstnumberx12.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">if</span><span id="lstnumberx12.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx12.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">actions</span><span id="lstnumberx12.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx12.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">is</span><span id="lstnumberx12.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx12.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">None</span>:

<div id="lstnumberx13" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx13.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">            </span><span id="lstnumberx13.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">break</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx14" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx14.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span><span id="lstnumberx14.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">computer</span>.<span id="lstnumberx14.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">step</span>(<span id="lstnumberx14.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">actions</span>)
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx15" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx15.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span><span id="lstnumberx15.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">history</span>.<span id="lstnumberx15.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">append</span>((<span id="lstnumberx15.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">observation</span>[”<span id="lstnumberx15.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">png</span>”],<span id="lstnumberx15.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx15.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">actions</span>))
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx16" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx16.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span><span id="lstnumberx16.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">computer</span>.<span id="lstnumberx16.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">done</span>()
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx17" class="ltx_listingline">
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx18" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx18.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">if</span><span id="lstnumberx18.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx18.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">__name__</span><span id="lstnumberx18.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>==<span id="lstnumberx18.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>”<span id="lstnumberx18.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">__main__</span>”:
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx19" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx19.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span><span id="lstnumberx19.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">run</span>(<span id="lstnumberx19.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">sys</span>.<span id="lstnumberx19.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">argv</span>[1],<span id="lstnumberx19.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx19.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">sys</span>.<span id="lstnumberx19.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">argv</span>[2])
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For example, an action list can contain
<span id="A3.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">{"mouse": {"left_click": [640, 400]}}</span> followed by
<span id="A3.SS2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">{"keyboard": {"text": "hello"}}</span>.
These two actions are executed in order within one step.
Convenience methods such as <span id="A3.SS2.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">click(640, 400)</span>,
<span id="A3.SS2.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">type_text("hello")</span>, and <span id="A3.SS2.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">keys(["ctrl", "c"])</span>
each submit a single action. The agent can execute several actions before
requesting another screenshot. Calling <span id="A3.SS2.p3.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">done()</span> ends the interaction;
the benchmark’s verifier determines the score.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.3 </span>Hosted and Local Evaluation</h3>

<div id="A3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Listing <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_label ltx_ref_self"></span> runs the Codex template on the
representative OSWorld set using Modal. The command specifies the
submission directory, benchmark, and number of parallel evaluations.
Omitting <span id="A3.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">--remote</span> runs both the agent and environment VMs on the
evaluator host. For local desktop evaluation, this must be a Linux host
with the VM runtime and hardware required by the benchmark, as well as
model-serving resources when using open-weight models.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<div id="A3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_listing ltx_lstlisting ltx_listing"><div class="ltx_listing_data"><a href="data:text/plain;base64,Y3VhLXNwZWVkcnVuIHJ1biAtLXJlbW90ZSBcCiAgICAtLXN1Ym1pc3Npb24gdGVtcGxhdGVzL2NvZGV4X2NsaSBcCiAgICAtLWJlbmNobWFyayBiZW5jaG1hcmtzL29zd29ybGQtZW5lcmd5NTAtcmVwcmVzZW50YXRpdmUgXAogICAgLS1hZ2VudHMtcGVyLWV2YWx1YXRpb24gMSAtLXBhcmFsbGVsLWV2YWx1YXRpb25zIDg=" download="">⬇</a></div>
<div id="lstnumberx20" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx20.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">cua</span>-<span id="lstnumberx20.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">speedrun</span><span id="lstnumberx20.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx20.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">run</span><span id="lstnumberx20.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>–<span id="lstnumberx20.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">remote</span><span id="lstnumberx20.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>\
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx21" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx21.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span>–<span id="lstnumberx21.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">submission</span><span id="lstnumberx21.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx21.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">templates</span>/<span id="lstnumberx21.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">codex_cli</span><span id="lstnumberx21.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>\
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx22" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx22.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span>–<span id="lstnumberx22.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">benchmark</span><span id="lstnumberx22.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx22.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">benchmarks</span>/<span id="lstnumberx22.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">osworld</span>-<span id="lstnumberx22.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">energy50</span>-<span id="lstnumberx22.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">representative</span><span id="lstnumberx22.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>\
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx23" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx23.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span>–<span id="lstnumberx23.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">agents</span>-<span id="lstnumberx23.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">per</span>-<span id="lstnumberx23.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">evaluation</span><span id="lstnumberx23.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>1<span id="lstnumberx23.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>–<span id="lstnumberx23.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">parallel</span>-<span id="lstnumberx23.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">evaluations</span><span id="lstnumberx23.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>8
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Users can also submit agents through the dashboard. For each evaluation,
we record the benchmark, hardware, evaluation settings, and task seeds,
along with task scores and timings. Action logs and screenshots allow
users to inspect how the agent completed or failed each task.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Interaction and Token Measurements</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Alongside performance, time, and cost, we measure how often an agent calls
its model, how many actions it executes, and how many tokens it generates.
These measurements support the analysis of agent speed in
Sec. <a href="#S3" title="3 Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>. The full configuration tables average over all
tasks, including unsuccessful attempts.</p>
</div>
<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Aggregate metrics.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For an agent <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> evaluated on <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> tasks, the mean verifier score <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math>,
mean task time <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math>, and mean model cost <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> are</p>
<table id="A4.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P(\pi)=\frac{1}{K}\sum_{i=1}^{K}r_{i},\qquad T(\pi)=\frac{1}{K}\sum_{i=1}^{K}t_{i},\qquad C(\pi)=\frac{1}{K}\sum_{i=1}^{K}c_{i}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>K</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></munderover><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>K</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></munderover><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>K</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>K</mi></munderover><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P(\pi)=\frac{1}{K}\sum_{i=1}^{K}r_{i},\qquad T(\pi)=\frac{1}{K}\sum_{i=1}^{K}t_{i},\qquad C(\pi)=\frac{1}{K}\sum_{i=1}^{K}c_{i},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the verifier score defined in
Appendix <a href="#A10.SS1" title="J.1 Task Definition ‣ Appendix J Experimental Details ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">J.1</span></a>, and <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> are the execution
time and model cost of task <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>. The mean score retains partial credit; we
also report the fraction of exactly completed tasks and the median time on
those tasks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Agent time, environment time, and requested waits.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We separate total task time into agent time and environment time.
For task <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, environment time <math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> sums the intervals recorded by the
environment server for executing actions and returning observations.
This includes explicit waits requested by the agent; we report their
requested durations separately and subtract them when reporting
environment time excluding agent waits. Agent time is the remainder,
<math id="A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{i}-e_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{i}-e_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, which includes model requests and agent-side processing.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>Model Calls, Action Batches, and Individual Actions</h3>

<section id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Model responses.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We count each completed model response, including responses without a
computer action. A response can contain several tool calls, each of
which may execute several actions. We therefore count model responses
and desktop actions separately.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Action batches and individual actions.</h5>

<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">An agent can execute several actions in one request. For example,
clicking a field, typing text, and pressing Enter in one request counts
as one batch and three actions. Issuing these actions separately counts
as three batches and three actions. A <em id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">step</em> denotes one request
containing keyboard, mouse, or wait actions. For task <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> batches, let
<math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{A}_{ij}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{A}_{ij}</annotation></semantics></math> be the action list in request <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>. The total number of
individual actions is <math id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{i}=\sum_{j=1}^{S_{i}}|\mathcal{A}_{ij}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒜</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{i}=\sum_{j=1}^{S_{i}}|\mathcal{A}_{ij}|</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We count actions as submitted by the agent: typing a string, pressing a
key combination, or requesting a wait each counts as one action.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.2 </span>Token Accounting</h3>

<div id="A4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We count every generated token once per response, including reasoning
and other output, using the provider’s reported usage. We also report
provider-supplied reasoning-token counts separately.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To compare token rates, we divide total generated tokens by total agent
time: <math id="A4.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{i}G_{i}/\sum_{i}(t_{i}-e_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>i</mi></msub><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">/</mo><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0em">∑</mo><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{i}G_{i}/\sum_{i}(t_{i}-e_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A4.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the generated-token
count for task <math id="A4.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>. This <em id="A4.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">effective token rate</em> includes the
time spent on model requests and agent-side processing.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.3 </span>Full Interaction and Token Comparisons</h3>

<div id="A4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Tables <a href="#A4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ D.3 Full Interaction and Token Comparisons ‣ Appendix D Interaction and Token Measurements ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> and <a href="#A4.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ D.3 Full Interaction and Token Comparisons ‣ Appendix D Interaction and Token Measurements ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>
report mean batches, individual actions, model responses, and generated
tokens for the configurations in Appendix <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Full Evaluation Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a>.
Configuration IDs match the frontier plots and result tables.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A4.T5" class="ltx_table">

<section id="A4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.4 </span>Performance–Interaction and Performance–Token Frontiers</h3>

<div id="A4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figures <a href="#A4.F7" title="Figure 7 ‣ D.3 Full Interaction and Token Comparisons ‣ Appendix D Interaction and Token Measurements ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>
and <a href="#A4.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ D.4 Performance–Interaction and Performance–Token Frontiers ‣ Appendix D Interaction and Token Measurements ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> compare performance with the
number of action batches, individual actions, and generated tokens on
OSWorld and OSWorld2. Circled points mark the Pareto frontier for each
metric. We use the same
trajectories as the time and cost comparisons and average over all tasks.</p>

<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Full Evaluation Results</h2>

<section id="A5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.1 </span>Model, Harness, and Reasoning-Effort Configurations</h3>

<div id="A5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Tables <a href="#A5.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ E.1 Model, Harness, and Reasoning-Effort Configurations ‣ Appendix E Full Evaluation Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>–<a href="#A5.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ E.1 Model, Harness, and Reasoning-Effort Configurations ‣ Appendix E Full Evaluation Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>
report mean score, time, cost, and token use for each model, harness,
and reasoning setting. Astra (low) uses five-seed means for each I/O setting.
The configuration IDs identify the corresponding points in the figures.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate Luna through both the direct API and Codex, and Kimi with
single-call and batched-call harnesses. We use the Yutori cookbook.</p>

<section id="A5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.2 </span>OSWorld: Performance–Time and Performance–Cost Frontiers</h3>

<div id="A5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A5.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ E.1 Model, Harness, and Reasoning-Effort Configurations ‣ Appendix E Full Evaluation Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> shows the full OSWorld comparison from
Figure <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ Metrics. ‣ 3.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 3 Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, with configuration IDs for all 56 points.</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">A common token-generation rate.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A5.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ E.1 Model, Harness, and Reasoning-Effort Configurations ‣ Appendix E Full Evaluation Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> compares measured task time with an
estimate that assigns every model the same generation rate. We compute
this estimate as recorded environment time plus generated tokens divided
by 100 tokens/s, using the same trajectories and scores. Opus 5 (low)
scores 87.6% in 85.9 s, while Astra (low) scores 90.8% in 89.5 s.
Opus generates 1,795 tokens per task compared with 1,579 for Astra.
With generation time assigned at the common rate,
Astra is faster. Environment time includes agent-requested waits
(Appendix <a href="#A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2" title="Agent time, environment time, and requested waits. ‣ Appendix D Interaction and Token Measurements ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<figure id="A5.F11" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2609.40284v1/results_full_median_green_review_20260925.svg" id="A5.F11.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:505/249;" width="505" height="249"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 11: </span><span id="A5.F11.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Full OSWorld median-time view and fast-region detail.</span>
Mean verifier score versus median task time for all 56 configurations.
For Astra (low), the median task times are averaged across five seeds.
The right plot enlarges the region containing the fastest configurations;
point IDs match the full OSWorld tables. Green dotted lines show the
published human references of 72.36% and 111.94 s from the original
369-task OSWorld benchmark <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xie et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A5.F12" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2609.40284v1/results_full_osworld2_green_kimi_review_20260925.svg" id="A5.F12.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:505/250;" width="505" height="250"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 12: </span><span id="A5.F12.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Full OSWorld2 performance–time and performance–cost comparisons.</span>
All 21 configurations are evaluated on the same 52 tasks.
Point IDs refer to the OSWorld2 configuration table. Marker shapes follow
Figure <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ Metrics. ‣ 3.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 3 Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>; darker green indicates greater reasoning
effort.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Median task time.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A5.F11" title="Figure 11 ‣ A common token-generation rate. ‣ E.2 OSWorld: Performance–Time and Performance–Cost Frontiers ‣ Appendix E Full Evaluation Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> reports median task time, which summarizes
the time for a typical task.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.3 </span>OSWorld2: Performance–Time and Performance–Cost Frontiers</h3>

<div id="A5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A5.F12" title="Figure 12 ‣ A common token-generation rate. ‣ E.2 OSWorld: Performance–Time and Performance–Cost Frontiers ‣ Appendix E Full Evaluation Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> compares all 21 OSWorld2 configurations.
Astra defines the entire time frontier, while Gemini 3.8 Flash and Muse
Spark 1.3 offer lower-cost choices on the cost frontier.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<figure id="A5.F13" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2609.40284v1/results_joint_frontier_osworld2_green_kimi_review_20260925.svg" id="A5.F13.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/302;" width="548" height="302"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 13: </span><span id="A5.F13.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Joint performance–time–cost frontier on OSWorld2.</span>
Circled points are the evaluated frontier configurations. Other configurations
appear in gray. Time and cost axes are logarithmic. Marker shapes follow
Figure <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ Metrics. ‣ 3.1 Experimental Setup ‣ 3 Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>; darker green indicates greater reasoning effort.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.4 </span>OSWorld2: Joint Performance–Time–Cost Frontier</h3>

<div id="A5.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A5.F13" title="Figure 13 ‣ E.3 OSWorld2: Performance–Time and Performance–Cost Frontiers ‣ Appendix E Full Evaluation Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a> extends the joint frontier in
Figure <a href="#S3.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 3.3 Practical Suggestions for Building CUAs ‣ 3 Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> to OSWorld2. A configuration is on
this frontier if no other evaluated configuration improves one of the
three metrics without worsening another. It includes Astra at all four
reasoning settings, Gemini 3.8 Flash at all three settings, and Muse
Spark 1.3 at minimal effort, allowing a choice based on the desired
score and the available time and cost budgets.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<figure id="A5.F14" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2609.40284v1/results_additional_benchmarks_green_20260923.svg" id="A5.F14.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:483/356;" width="483" height="356"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 14: </span><span id="A5.F14.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Performance–time and performance–cost frontiers on MyPCBench and CUA-World.</span>
GPT-6 Astra through Codex at four reasoning settings. Each point averages
the same 38 MyPCBench tasks (top) or 26 CUA-World tasks (bottom).
Darker green indicates greater reasoning effort. Dashed lines connect
the observed Pareto-frontier points, which are circled.</figcaption>
</figure>

<section id="A5.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.5 </span>Reasoning Effort on MyPCBench</h3>

<div id="A5.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A5.F14" title="Figure 14 ‣ E.4 OSWorld2: Joint Performance–Time–Cost Frontier ‣ Appendix E Full Evaluation Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a> and
Table <a href="#A5.T10" title="Table 10 ‣ E.4 OSWorld2: Joint Performance–Time–Cost Frontier ‣ Appendix E Full Evaluation Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> compare GPT-6 Astra through Codex at
four reasoning settings on MyPCBench. Xhigh achieves the highest score,
93.6%, while medium has the lowest mean time and cost, 495 s and
$4.33 per task. We evaluate the 38-task representative
set from Sec. <a href="#S2.SS2" title="2.2 Selecting a Representative Set ‣ 2 Method ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>, with a limit of 100 action
batches. All reported means include
unsuccessful tasks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.6 </span>Reasoning Effort on CUA-World</h3>

<div id="A5.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A5.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A5.F14" title="Figure 14 ‣ E.4 OSWorld2: Joint Performance–Time–Cost Frontier ‣ Appendix E Full Evaluation Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a> and
Table <a href="#A5.T10" title="Table 10 ‣ E.4 OSWorld2: Joint Performance–Time–Cost Frontier ‣ Appendix E Full Evaluation Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> show a different outcome on
CUA-World. High effort scores 94.2%, compared
with 93.0% at xhigh, while taking less time (1,108 vs. 1,515 s)
and costing less ($11.11 vs. $15.06 per task).
All four settings use Astra through Codex on the same 26 long-horizon
tasks, with a limit of 500 action batches.</p>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Run-to-Run Variation</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We repeat the evaluation across five seeds to measure variation in
scores, task times, and action sequences. We also compare scores on
individual tasks to determine whether the same tasks succeed across
runs. Appendix <a href="#A2.SS6" title="B.6 Fast I/O Consistency Across Five Seeds ‣ Appendix B Infrastructure: Technical Details ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.6</span></a> reports the corresponding
timing results for Fast I/O.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.1 </span>Five-Seed Evaluation Setup</h3>

<div id="A6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate GPT-6 Astra at low reasoning effort using Codex on the
same 50 OSWorld tasks. Each run uses the same agent prompt and a
500-step limit. Only the task seed changes.</p>
</div>

<section id="A6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.2 </span>Scores and Times Across Seeds</h3>

<div id="A6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A6.T11" title="Table 11 ‣ F.1 Five-Seed Evaluation Setup ‣ Appendix F Run-to-Run Variation ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a> shows that both score and task time vary
little across seeds. Mean task time is <math id="A6.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="89.54\pm 2.16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>89.54</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>2.16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">89.54\pm 2.16</annotation></semantics></math> s, and the score is
<math id="A6.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="90.82\pm 1.79" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>90.82</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>1.79</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">90.82\pm 1.79</annotation></semantics></math>% (mean <math id="A6.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> standard deviation).
The mean number of action batches is also stable at <math id="A6.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.86\pm 0.06" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5.86</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.06</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.86\pm 0.06</annotation></semantics></math>
per task.
Timing components are defined in Appendix <a href="#A4.SS0.SSS0.Px2" title="Agent time, environment time, and requested waits. ‣ Appendix D Interaction and Token Measurements ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 12: </span><span id="A6.T12.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Task-level repeatability across five seeds of Astra at low effort.</span> Values average uniformly over all size-<math id="A6.T12.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> subsets of the five runs, then over the 50 tasks. Pass@<math id="A6.T12.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> measures whether any of the <math id="A6.T12.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> attempts succeeds; best-of-<math id="A6.T12.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> uses the highest partial score.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A6.T12" title="Table 12 ‣ F.3 Task-Level Score Agreement ‣ Appendix F Run-to-Run Variation ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> shows that additional attempts improve
performance only slightly. With standard I/O, 42 tasks receive full
credit in all five runs, two in four runs, and six in none.
Partial-credit scores are identical across all five runs on 48 of the
50 tasks. The low variation in mean score therefore reflects
consistent performance on individual tasks: almost every task receives
the same score on every attempt. With Fast I/O, 40 tasks receive full
credit in all five runs, four in four runs, one in one run, and five
in none. Partial-credit scores are identical on 45 tasks.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Pass@<math id="A6.SS3.SSS0.Px1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> and partial credit.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For a task with <math id="A6.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> fully successful runs among the five, the probability
that a uniformly selected set of <math id="A6.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> runs contains a success is
<math id="A6.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\binom{5-c}{k}/\binom{5}{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0pt"><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mi>k</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac linethickness="0pt"><mn>5</mn><mi>k</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\binom{5-c}{k}/\binom{5}{k}</annotation></semantics></math>. Pass@<math id="A6.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> averages this quantity over
tasks. For partial credit, the table averages the maximum
task score within each size-<math id="A6.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> set. Standard-I/O pass@1 is 87.2%
and pass@5 is 88.0%; its best-of-five partial score is 91.62%.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.4 </span>Variation in Action Sequences</h3>

<div id="A6.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We next compare the number of action batches used for the same task
across seeds. For each task, we compute the standard deviation and
range across its five trajectories. With standard I/O, the median of
these task-level standard deviations is 0.55 batches, and the median
range is one batch. For Fast I/O, the corresponding values are 0.99
and two batches.</p>
</div>
<section id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Two ways to complete the same spreadsheet task.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For example, on the Calc task that cleans movie titles, all five
standard-I/O runs receive full credit while taking 7, 6, 5, 6, and
2 batches.
The seven-batch trajectory enters separate
<span id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">PROPER(TRIM(...))</span> formulas for successive rows and revisits
the paste-special dialog. The two-batch trajectory selects
<span id="A6.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">C2:C29</span>, enters one formula with Alt+Enter to fill the
selection, then saves. The two trajectories take 97.4 and 40.3 s,
respectively. Here, the agent reduces the number of batches by
applying the formula to all rows at once.</p>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Representative Task Selection</h2>

<div id="A7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We select a small set of tasks from each benchmark to reduce evaluation
time while preserving the scores and relative performance of agents.
This section gives the selection procedure from
Sec. <a href="#S2.SS2" title="2.2 Selecting a Representative Set ‣ 2 Method ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a> and
tests its score estimates, rankings, and speed–performance frontier
on held-out models.
Table <a href="#A7.T13" title="Table 13 ‣ Appendix G Representative Task Selection ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a> lists the resulting task counts.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A7.T13" class="ltx_table">
<table id="A7.T13.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="A7.T13.2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A7.T13.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt">Benchmark</th>
<th id="A7.T13.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt">Full set</th>
<th id="A7.T13.2.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt">Selected subset</th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="A7.T13.2.2" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="A7.T13.2.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_t">OSWorld <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xie et al., 2024</a>)</cite></th>
<td id="A7.T13.2.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_t">295</td>

<section id="A7.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.1 </span>Models and Tasks Used for Selection</h3>

<section id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">OSWorld.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use nine configurations evaluated on the same
295 tasks: Claude Sonnet 5 xhigh, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Gemini 3 Flash Preview,
GLM-5V Turbo, GPT-5.6 Luna xhigh, Kimi K3, Meta Muse Spark, MiniMax M3,
and Qwen3.5-9B-Thinking. Each task is represented by its nine partial
scores and nine exact-completion indicators. The internet-dependence
audit defining this task population is described in
Appendix <a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Internet-Dependence Audit ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">OSWorld2.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Selection uses seven configurations:
MiniMax-M3, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Sonnet 4.6 at medium and maximum
effort, GPT-5.5, GPT-5.6, and Qwen3.7. The resulting evaluation set
contains 52 tasks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">CUA-World.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Selection uses seven configurations with scores on more
than 30 tasks each: Qwen3-VL-2B-Thinking, GPT-5.4 through Azure,
GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 3 Flash Preview,
and Kimi K2.5. Selection uses each model’s distribution of observed
partial scores. Repeated runs remain separate observations. The
selected set contains 26 tasks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">MyPCBench.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The evaluation uses 38 of the 184 canonical tasks, selected with the
unweighted energy method and 100 initializations. The task identities
for all four benchmarks are listed in
Appendix <a href="#A7.SS6" title="G.6 Selected Task Identities ‣ Appendix G Representative Task Selection ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">G.6</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.2 </span>Initialization, Optimization, and Task Count</h3>

<div id="A7.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We seek a subset that represents the full benchmark’s distribution of
score patterns. For
OSWorld and OSWorld2, let <math id="A7.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> concatenate the partial
scores and exact-completion indicators for task <math id="A7.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>. Distances are
<math id="A7.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{ij}=\lVert z_{i}-z_{j}\rVert_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><msub><mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0em">∥</mo><mrow><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em">∥</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{ij}=\lVert z_{i}-z_{j}\rVert_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. For a subset <math id="A7.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> of size <math id="A7.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> from
<math id="A7.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> tasks, the normalized energy objective is</p>
<table id="A7.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E(S)=\frac{1}{\bar{d}}\left[\frac{2}{KN}\sum_{i\in S}\sum_{j=1}^{N}d_{ij}-\frac{1}{K^{2}}\sum_{i,j\in S}d_{ij}-\frac{1}{N^{2}}\sum_{i,j=1}^{N}d_{ij}\right],\qquad\bar{d}=\frac{\sum_{i\neq j}d_{ij}}{N(N-1)}." display="block"
