movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>K</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></munder><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>d</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E(S)=\frac{1}{\bar{d}}\left[\frac{2}{KN}\sum_{i\in S}\sum_{j=1}^{N}d_{ij}-\frac{1}{K^{2}}\sum_{i,j\in S}d_{ij}-\frac{1}{N^{2}}\sum_{i,j=1}^{N}d_{ij}\right],\qquad\bar{d}=\frac{\sum_{i\neq j}d_{ij}}{N(N-1)}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A7.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">We estimate a model’s benchmark score by its unweighted mean score
on the selected tasks.</p>
</div>
<section id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Balanced initializations.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To cover a range of score profiles in each initial subset, we sort
tasks by the leading principal coordinate of their centered
score profiles and choose evenly spaced tasks from this ordering.
Specifically, for a uniformly sampled phase <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi\in[0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi\in[0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, the
initial positions are <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lfloor(\phi+t)N/K\rfloor" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌊</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌋</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lfloor(\phi+t)N/K\rfloor</annotation></semantics></math> for
<math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=0,\ldots,K-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=0,\ldots,K-1</annotation></semantics></math>. We use 100 initializations with seeds
<math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7000,\ldots,7099" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>7000</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>7099</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7000,\ldots,7099</annotation></semantics></math>, optimizing each distinct initial subset once.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">One-swap optimization.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At each iteration, we evaluate every exchange of a selected task with
an unselected task and apply the exchange that reduces energy the most.
We stop when no exchange improves the objective beyond numerical
tolerance and retain the lowest-energy subset across the initializations.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_listing ltx_lstlisting ltx_listing"><div class="ltx_listing_data"><a href="data:text/plain;base64," download="">⬇</a></div>
<div id="lstnumberx24" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx24.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">for</span><span id="lstnumberx24.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx24.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">each</span><span id="lstnumberx24.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx24.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">candidate</span><span id="lstnumberx24.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx24.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">task</span><span id="lstnumberx24.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx24.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">count</span><span id="lstnumberx24.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx24.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">K</span>:
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx25" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx25.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span><span id="lstnumberx25.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">for</span><span id="lstnumberx25.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx25.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">each</span><span id="lstnumberx25.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx25.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">model</span><span id="lstnumberx25.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx25.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">h</span>:
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx26" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx26.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span><span id="lstnumberx26.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">remove</span><span id="lstnumberx26.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx26.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">model</span><span id="lstnumberx26.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx26.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">h</span><span id="lstnumberx26.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx26.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">from</span><span id="lstnumberx26.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx26.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">the</span><span id="lstnumberx26.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx26.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">calibration</span><span id="lstnumberx26.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx26.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">models</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx27" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx27.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span><span id="lstnumberx27.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">form</span><span id="lstnumberx27.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx27.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">task</span><span id="lstnumberx27.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx27.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">profiles</span><span id="lstnumberx27.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx27.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">from</span><span id="lstnumberx27.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx27.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">the</span><span id="lstnumberx27.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx27.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">remaining</span><span id="lstnumberx27.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx27.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">models</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx28" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx28.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span><span id="lstnumberx28.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">optimize</span><span id="lstnumberx28.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>100<span id="lstnumberx28.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx28.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">balanced</span><span id="lstnumberx28.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx28.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">initial</span><span id="lstnumberx28.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx28.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">subsets</span><span id="lstnumberx28.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx28.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">by</span><span id="lstnumberx28.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx28.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">one</span>-<span id="lstnumberx28.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">task</span><span id="lstnumberx28.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx28.16" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">swaps</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx29" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx29.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span><span id="lstnumberx29.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">select</span><span id="lstnumberx29.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx29.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">the</span><span id="lstnumberx29.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx29.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">subset</span><span id="lstnumberx29.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx29.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">with</span><span id="lstnumberx29.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx29.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">the</span><span id="lstnumberx29.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx29.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">lowest</span><span id="lstnumberx29.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx29.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">calibration</span><span id="lstnumberx29.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx29.16" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">energy</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx30" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx30.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">        </span><span id="lstnumberx30.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">predict</span><span id="lstnumberx30.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx30.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">h</span>’<span id="lstnumberx30.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">s</span><span id="lstnumberx30.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx30.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">partial</span><span id="lstnumberx30.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx30.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">and</span><span id="lstnumberx30.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx30.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">exact</span><span id="lstnumberx30.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx30.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">scores</span><span id="lstnumberx30.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx30.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">by</span><span id="lstnumberx30.16" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx30.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">subset</span><span id="lstnumberx30.18" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx30.19" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">means</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx31" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx31.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space">    </span><span id="lstnumberx31.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">compare</span><span id="lstnumberx31.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx31.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">predictions</span><span id="lstnumberx31.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx31.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">with</span><span id="lstnumberx31.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx31.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">each</span><span id="lstnumberx31.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx31.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">model</span>’<span id="lstnumberx31.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">s</span><span id="lstnumberx31.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx31.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">full</span>-<span id="lstnumberx31.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">set</span><span id="lstnumberx31.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx31.16" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">means</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx32" class="ltx_listingline">
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx33" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx33.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">choose</span><span id="lstnumberx33.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx33.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">the</span><span id="lstnumberx33.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx33.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">smallest</span><span id="lstnumberx33.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx33.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">K</span><span id="lstnumberx33.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx33.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">for</span><span id="lstnumberx33.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx33.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">which</span><span id="lstnumberx33.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx33.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">both</span><span id="lstnumberx33.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx33.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">rank</span><span id="lstnumberx33.16" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx33.17" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">correlations</span>
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx34" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx34.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">are</span><span id="lstnumberx34.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx34.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">at</span><span id="lstnumberx34.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx34.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">least</span><span id="lstnumberx34.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span>0.95<span id="lstnumberx34.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx34.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">at</span><span id="lstnumberx34.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx34.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">K</span>-1,<span id="lstnumberx34.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx34.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">K</span>,<span id="lstnumberx34.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx34.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">and</span><span id="lstnumberx34.15" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx34.16" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">K</span>+1
</div>
<div id="lstnumberx35" class="ltx_listingline"><span id="lstnumberx35.1" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">refit</span><span id="lstnumberx35.2" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx35.3" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">the</span><span id="lstnumberx35.4" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx35.5" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">K</span>-<span id="lstnumberx35.6" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">task</span><span id="lstnumberx35.7" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx35.8" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">subset</span><span id="lstnumberx35.9" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx35.10" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">using</span><span id="lstnumberx35.11" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx35.12" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">all</span><span id="lstnumberx35.13" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_space"> </span><span id="lstnumberx35.14" class="ltx_text ltx_lst_identifier">models</span>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To choose the number of tasks, we repeat the full selection procedure
with each model held out in turn
(Listing <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_label ltx_ref_self"></span>). We construct task profiles and select
tasks using the remaining models, then compare the held-out model’s
subset score with its full-set score. We choose the smallest <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> for
which both partial-score and exact-completion rank correlations are
at least 0.95 at <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K-1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K+1</annotation></semantics></math>. Checking the neighboring task
counts tests the stability of the ranking criterion. Each
task count is optimized independently. After choosing <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>, we select the final evaluation set
using all models.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Selection with missing scores.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Some CUA-World models have scores on only part of the benchmark. We
therefore compare each model’s distribution of observed partial scores
on selected tasks with its distribution over all observed tasks,
using one-dimensional energy distance. We first ensure that the subset
contains an observation for every model used for selection, then
minimize the mean of these distances. The task-count rule uses partial-score rank correlation
at <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K-1,K,K+1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K-1,K,K+1</annotation></semantics></math>.
At <math id="A7.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=25,26,27" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>26</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>27</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=25,26,27</annotation></semantics></math>, the seven-model held-out correlations are
0.964, 1.000, and 1.000, respectively; the corresponding score errors
are 7.43, 5.12, and 2.10 percentage points. These errors compare
unweighted means of observed run scores.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<figure id="A7.F15" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2609.40284v1/appendix_selection_validation.svg" id="A7.F15.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/380;" width="548" height="380"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 15: </span><span id="A7.F15.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Score error and rank correlation on held-out models.</span>
OSWorld uses nine leave-one-agent-out folds; OSWorld2 uses seven.
The randomized baseline averages 300 difficulty-stratified selections
per task count. Dotted vertical lines mark 50 and 52 tasks; horizontal
lines mark rank correlation 0.95. Each task count is optimized
independently.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.3 </span>Held-Out Score and Ranking Accuracy</h3>

<div id="A7.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A7.F15" title="Figure 15 ‣ Selection with missing scores. ‣ G.2 Initialization, Optimization, and Task Count ‣ Appendix G Representative Task Selection ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a> compares energy-based selection
with a randomized baseline that samples tasks across
difficulty levels. We measure error as the mean absolute difference
between each held-out model’s subset estimate and its full-set result.
At 50 OSWorld tasks, energy-based selection reduces
partial-score error from 4.02 to 2.16 percentage points. It also
reduces mean-task-time error from 51.0 to 31.4 s, even though
selection uses only scores. Thus, selecting tasks with representative
score patterns also improves estimates of execution time.</p>
</div>

<div id="A7.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A7.T14" title="Table 14 ‣ G.3 Held-Out Score and Ranking Accuracy ‣ Appendix G Representative Task Selection ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">14</span></a> shows that the selected task sets
closely preserve model rankings on both benchmarks. At 50 tasks, OSWorld

<section id="A7.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.4 </span>Preserving the Speed–Performance Frontier</h3>

<div id="A7.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A7.F16" title="Figure 16 ‣ G.3 Held-Out Score and Ranking Accuracy ‣ Appendix G Representative Task Selection ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a> compares the full-set frontier with
the frontier estimated from 50-task subsets for held-out models. The
estimated frontier recovers two of the three full-set frontier
configurations and adds no others, giving 100% precision and 66.7%
recall. Pairwise dominance agrees for 91.7% of model pairs. This analysis
uses the models’ scores and times; selection itself uses only scores.</p>
</div>
<section id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Evaluation savings.</h5>

<div id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Selecting 50 of the 295 OSWorld tasks reduces the number of tasks by
<math id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="5.9\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5.9</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5.9\times</annotation></semantics></math>. Across the nine models, these tasks account
for 15.1% of the total recorded task time, a <math id="A7.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="6.61\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6.61</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.61\times</annotation></semantics></math> reduction.
We compute this saving by summing trajectory times, excluding setup
and verification.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<figure id="A7.T15" class="ltx_table">
<table id="A7.T15.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">

</section>
<section id="A7.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.5 </span>Comparing Task-Selection Methods</h3>

<div id="A7.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A7.T15" title="Table 15 ‣ Evaluation savings. ‣ G.4 Preserving the Speed–Performance Frontier ‣ Appendix G Representative Task Selection ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a> compares task-selection methods at a
budget of 32 OSWorld tasks, using the same nine leave-one-agent-out
folds. Energy-based selection achieves a mean error of 4.42 percentage
points, compared to 5.08 for difficulty-stratified random selection and
8.08 for the IRT-inspired method.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We use energy-based selection for its simple scoring rule: each agent’s
benchmark score is the average of its scores on the selected tasks.
The IRT-inspired method fits a one-parameter ability model
using the eight agents available in each fold and predicts full-benchmark
performance from the selected-task scores.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.6 </span>Selected Task Identities</h3>

<div id="A7.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A7.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The following lists give the final task sets used in our evaluations.
OSWorld IDs use the original task UUIDs. OSWorld2 uses its three-digit identifiers;
MyPCBench IDs combine the task family and suffix; CUA-World IDs combine
the environment and task name.</p>
</div>

<section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>Internet-Dependence Audit</h2>

<div id="A8.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Live public services can change their content, become unavailable, or
restrict access between evaluations. We therefore audit whether each
task requires the agent to use such services. Tasks that use a local
application or a benchmark-controlled website remain eligible, as do
tasks that only require downloading fixed files during setup.</p>
</div>
<section id="A8.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.1 </span>Inclusion Rule</h3>

<div id="A8.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We first use a coding agent to classify the 369 OSWorld tasks as
local/offline, benign internet, or anti-bot/access-sensitive. Three
human reviewers then independently assess whether each task requires
interaction with a live public service. We include a task only when
all three reviewers agree to include it. This gives 295 tasks.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A8.T18" class="ltx_table">
<table id="A8.T18.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">

The seven disagreements are excluded by the unanimous-inclusion rule.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">H.2 </span>Reviewer Agreement</h3>

<div id="A8.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A8.T18" title="Table 18 ‣ H.1 Inclusion Rule ‣ Appendix H Internet-Dependence Audit ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a> shows that 362 of 369 tasks receive a
unanimous decision. Pairwise agreement is 98.64%, 99.46%, and 98.10%
for reviewer pairs 1–2, 1–3, and 2–3, respectively. Their Cohen’s
<math id="A8.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> values are 0.956, 0.983, and 0.939; Fleiss’ <math id="A8.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math> across
all three reviewers is 0.959.</p>
</div>
<section id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Applying the criterion across benchmarks.</h5>

<div id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A8.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We apply the same criterion to the other benchmarks. OSWorld2 provides
benchmark-controlled web applications, and MyPCBench provides local,
pre-authenticated services, so these tasks remain eligible. For
CUA-World, we exclude tasks requiring internet access during agent
interaction while retaining those that only use the network for setup.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A9" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix I </span>Validating Actions with CUA-AutoDebug</h2>

<div id="A9.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A task can fail because the model chooses an incorrect action or because
the infrastructure executes a correct action incorrectly. We developed
CUA-AutoDebug to distinguish these errors. A controlled desktop
application records the keyboard and mouse inputs it receives, including
modifier keys and typed text. We also check the resulting application
state: a click should reach the intended target, a drag should move the
object, and typed text should match the requested string. For shortcuts
handled by the operating system, we record input events before they reach
the application.</p>
</div>
<section id="A9.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">I.1 </span>Separating Model, Harness, and Runtime Errors</h3>

<div id="A9.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We first submit predefined actions directly to the VM runtime.
We then test agent harnesses by giving the model a short instruction,
such as clicking a colored square, and comparing its response with the
executed action and received input. An incorrect model action is a model
error; incorrect translation of a correct action is a harness error.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A9.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">I.2 </span>Input Failures Detected by the Runtime Tests</h3>

<td id="A9.T19.2.6.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;">
<span id="A9.T19.2.6.1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:91.4pt;">
<span id="A9.T19.2.6.1.1.1" class="ltx_p">Toggle Caps Lock, then type</span>
</span></td>
<td id="A9.T19.2.6.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;">
<span id="A9.T19.2.6.2.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:135.1pt;">
<span id="A9.T19.2.6.2.1.1" class="ltx_p">Lowercase text</span>
</span></td>
<td id="A9.T19.2.6.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_align_top ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;">
<span id="A9.T19.2.6.3.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_top" style="width:127.2pt;">
<span id="A9.T19.2.6.3.1.1" class="ltx_p">Caps Lock press silently omitted</span>
</span></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 19: </span><span id="A9.T19.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Input errors detected by CUA-AutoDebug when executing
actions through SSH and PyAutoGUI.</span> The tests compare requested input
with the keyboard and mouse events received.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A9.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A9.T19" title="Table 19 ‣ I.2 Input Failures Detected by the Runtime Tests ‣ Appendix I Validating Actions with CUA-AutoDebug ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">19</span></a> shows examples of input errors detected
by these tests, such as typing <span id="A9.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">&gt;</span> when <span id="A9.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">&lt;</span> was requested or
silently dropping accented characters. We test a catalog of 100 cases
covering clicks, drags, scrolls, key presses, key combinations, text entry,
and sequences of these actions. Six cases are unsupported by the tested
action interface. We repeat each of the remaining 94 cases five times;
83 pass and 11 fail when executed through SSH and PyAutoGUI. The failures
include one shell-expansion case, one shifted-symbol case, five Unicode
cases, and four named-key cases.</p>
</div>
<section id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The corrected runtime passes all 470 tests.</h5>

<div id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We correct these errors in CUA-Speedrun’s QEMU runtime by preserving
literal text when sending commands, explicitly mapping key names and
modifiers, and supporting characters absent from the default keyboard
mapping. After these corrections, all 94 supported cases pass in all
five repetitions.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 20: </span><span id="A9.T20.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Harness errors can change a correct model action.</span>
Examples detected by comparing model responses with the actions
executed and the input events received.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A9.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A9.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A9.T20" title="Table 20 ‣ I.3 Failures in Agent Harnesses ‣ Appendix I Validating Actions with CUA-AutoDebug ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">20</span></a> shows that harness errors can
prevent a correct model response from reaching the application. For
example, the Gemini harness reversed scroll direction and interpreted a
fallback scroll distance in pixels as a number of wheel ticks. All six
scroll-direction test repetitions failed before correction and passed
afterward. The Qwen3.5 harness released the modifier key before a click
and silently discarded tool calls after the first. A model that described
a triple-click but emitted a double-click produced a model error.</p>
</div>

<section id="A10" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix J </span>Experimental Details</h2>

<div id="A10.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Appendix <a href="#A5.SS1" title="E.1 Model, Harness, and Reasoning-Effort Configurations ‣ Appendix E Full Evaluation Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.1</span></a>
lists the model, harness, and reasoning setting for each configuration.</p>
</div>
<section id="A10.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">J.1 </span>Task Definition</h3>

<div id="A10.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We define a computer-use task as <math id="A10.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i}=(E_{i},s_{i}^{0},p_{i},V_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i}=(E_{i},s_{i}^{0},p_{i},V_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A10.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is
an interactive environment with initial state <math id="A10.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{i}^{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{i}^{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A10.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is a
natural-language instruction, and <math id="A10.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is a verification function. An
agent <math id="A10.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> receives <math id="A10.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and a sequence of observations and produces
computer actions until it terminates or reaches the task limit. This
interaction produces a trajectory <math id="A10.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and final state <math id="A10.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{i}^{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>T</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s_{i}^{T}</annotation></semantics></math>, with
score <math id="A10.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{i}=V_{i}(\tau_{i},s_{i}^{T})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>τ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>T</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{i}=V_{i}(\tau_{i},s_{i}^{T})</annotation></semantics></math>. A benchmark <math id="A10.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B=\{x_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B=\{x_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math> is a
collection of such tasks.</p>
</div>
<section id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Agent implementations.</h5>

<div id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We connect each model’s public reference agent or native computer-use API
to the common desktop interface.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A10.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">J.2 </span>Observations, Actions, and Interaction History</h3>

<div id="A10.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The environment provides <math id="A10.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1920\times 1080" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1920</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1080</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1920\times 1080</annotation></semantics></math> screenshots of the desktop.
Mouse actions use pixel coordinates in these images.
Harnesses that resize screenshots or use normalized coordinates convert
the model’s coordinates to desktop pixels before executing an action.</p>
</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 21: </span><span id="A10.T21.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Desktop actions supported by the infrastructure.</span> A batch
contains one or more actions executed in order. The model-facing
tool schema can differ between harnesses.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A10.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A10.T21" title="Table 21 ‣ J.2 Observations, Actions, and Interaction History ‣ Appendix J Experimental Details ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">21</span></a> lists the actions available to agents.
Direct-API agents translate the model’s computer-use responses into these
actions and return screenshots in the provider’s tool-result format.
Codex uses the same actions from a separate agent sandbox. We instruct
Codex to interact with the task desktop only through the supplied
interface: its local shell and files belong to the agent sandbox
(Listing <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_label ltx_ref_self"></span>).</p>
</div>

</div>
</div>
</div>
<section id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Interaction history.</h5>

<div id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each harness determines which screenshots and previous responses remain
in the model’s context. Kimi’s harness retains the current
screenshot and the two most recent completed-turn screenshots.
Earlier turns are compacted into textual history; recent responses
retain their reasoning fields and tool calls.
Codex maintains its own interaction history and explicitly retrieves
screenshots.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reasoning settings.</h5>

<div id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We vary reasoning effort within each model using the settings exposed by
its provider, such as low and high.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A10.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">J.3 </span>Task Limits and Execution</h3>

<div id="A10.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Each evaluation fixes the task set, agent implementation, reasoning
setting, environment resources, and number of parallel tasks. Every task
starts from its benchmark-specified initial state. We measure task time
from when the instruction is given to the agent until it terminates or
reaches the task limit, excluding setup, initialization, and verification
(Sec. <a href="#S2.SS1" title="2.1 Standardized Computer-Use Evaluation ‣ 2 Method ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<section id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Time and action limits.</h5>

<div id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The OSWorld and OSWorld2 configurations in Appendix <a href="#A5.SS1" title="E.1 Model, Harness, and Reasoning-Effort Configurations ‣ Appendix E Full Evaluation Results ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.1</span></a>
have an environment deadline of 39,600 s per task, while the MyPCBench
Astra sweep uses 7,200 s. These deadlines apply separately from the harness’s action or
model-turn limit and the timeout on an individual model request.</p>
</div>
<div id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We allow 500 action batches per task in the Astra batching comparison,
five-seed experiments, and CUA-World sweep, and 100 in the MyPCBench
sweep. A batch can contain several actions before the next observation;
the single-action Astra ablation requires a screenshot after
every action (Appendix <a href="#A11.SS1" title="K.1 Controlled Batching Comparisons ‣ Appendix K Additional Agent Analyses ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">K.1</span></a>). In the Fast I/O comparison,
we keep the model and reasoning setting fixed and change the action and
screenshot implementation (Appendix <a href="#A2.SS3" title="B.3 Fast I/O Implementation ‣ Appendix B Infrastructure: Technical Details ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.3</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A10.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">J.4 </span>Benchmark Verification</h3>

<div id="A10.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use each benchmark’s verification procedure. OSWorld and OSWorld2
score task completion with task-specific programmatic checks. CUA-World
uses Gemini 3 Flash Preview to assess the recorded trajectory against
its visual checklist. MyPCBench uses its visual trajectory judge and
averages the rubric scores with equal weight; a task receives full
credit only when every rubric passes. We also retain each benchmark’s
task instructions and context, including MyPCBench’s persona and
pre-authenticated local applications, alongside the agent’s system prompt.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A10.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">J.5 </span>Model Cost</h3>

<div id="A10.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compute model cost by summing the cost of each task’s model
requests. Each request’s cost comes from the provider’s recorded charge
or its recorded token usage at the applicable API prices.
Generated tokens follow the accounting in
Appendix <a href="#A4.SS2" title="D.2 Token Accounting ‣ Appendix D Interaction and Token Measurements ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A10.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A10.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Model cost excludes environment hosting, model-server
rental, setup, and separate verification calls.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A11" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix K </span>Additional Agent Analyses</h2>

<div id="A11.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A11.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We examine how action batching, agent harnesses, and reasoning effort
affect task time through comparisons within the same model. Action
batches, individual actions, and generated tokens are defined in
Appendix <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Interaction and Token Measurements ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A11.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">K.1 </span>Controlled Batching Comparisons</h3>

<section id="A11.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Batching makes Astra faster at the same score.</h5>

<div id="A11.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A11.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A11.T22" title="Table 22 ‣ K.1 Controlled Batching Comparisons ‣ Appendix K Additional Agent Analyses ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">22</span></a> compares Astra xhigh with its standard
batched actions and a restriction to one action between screenshots.
Both settings score 91.62%, but the single-action setting takes
182.7 s per task compared with 126.8 s for batching. It executes fewer
individual actions (16.50 versus 19.90), yet requires more action batches
(16.50 versus 7.14) and generates more tokens (2,559 versus 2,060).
We keep the model, reasoning effort, 50-task set, and configured limits
fixed. To enforce the single-action restriction, we reject multi-action
requests and prevent further actions until the agent retrieves a new
screenshot, including actions issued in separate back-to-back requests.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A11.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Kimi benefits from batched tools at some reasoning settings.</h5>

<div id="A11.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A11.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A11.T22" title="Table 22 ‣ K.1 Controlled Batching Comparisons ‣ Appendix K Additional Agent Analyses ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">22</span></a> also compares Kimi at matched low,
high, and maximum effort. Kimi’s single-tool setting disables parallel
tool calls and allows
multiple GUI actions within one code block. At maximum effort, batched
tools reduce mean task time from 606.3 to 443.7 s and improve the score
from 85.62% to 89.62%. At high effort, batching increases time
from 305.1 to 358.1 s while reducing the score from 81.62% to 79.62%.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<figure id="A11.F17" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2609.40284v1/results_harness_full_green_20260921.svg" id="A11.F17.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/217;" width="548" height="217"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 17: </span><span id="A11.F17.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Harness performance depends on reasoning effort.</span>
GPT-5.6 Luna at low, medium, and high reasoning effort, using the
direct-API agent or Codex on OSWorld. Each curve connects reasoning
settings within one harness. All six evaluations use the same 50-task set.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A11.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">K.2 </span>Harness Comparisons Across Reasoning Efforts</h3>

<div id="A11.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A11.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A11.F17" title="Figure 17 ‣ Kimi benefits from batched tools at some reasoning settings. ‣ K.1 Controlled Batching Comparisons ‣ Appendix K Additional Agent Analyses ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a> compares GPT-5.6 Luna with Codex
and the direct-API agent at low, medium, and high effort. At low effort,
Codex improves the score from 61.8% to 75.6% but increases mean task
time from 74 to 145 s. At medium and high effort, the direct-API agent
is both more accurate and faster: it scores 75.6% in 119 s compared
with 67.6% in 189 s at medium, and 81.6% in 161 s compared with
79.6% in 325 s at high.</p>
</div>
</section>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 23: </span><span id="A11.T23.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Reasoning effort on tasks completed fully at every compared effort on OSWorld2.</span> Every reported score is 100%. Time is in seconds per task; token rate divides total generated tokens by total agent time. Each model uses its own common task set.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="A11.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Higher effort can generate longer outputs and more actions on the same successful tasks.</h5>

<div id="A11.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A11.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A11.T23" title="Table 23 ‣ K.3 Comparing Reasoning Efforts on the Same Successful Tasks ‣ Appendix K Additional Agent Analyses ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a> restricts each OSWorld2 comparison to
tasks that receive full credit at every evaluated effort for that model.
On the five tasks that Gemini 3.8 Flash completes at all three efforts,
high effort takes 3,024 s per task compared with 1,291 s at low effort.
It generates more than twice as many tokens (73,578 versus 29,596) and
executes more actions and batches. In comparison, its effective token
rate falls from 47.57 to 42.18 tokens/s.</p>
</div>
<div id="A11.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A11.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We observe a similar increase at Astra’s highest effort. On the 13 tasks
it completes at all four settings, xhigh takes 1,132 s, compared with
792 s at low and 753 s at medium. It generates 14,359 tokens and
executes 223 actions, compared with 7,878 tokens and 147 actions at low
effort. Muse Spark 1.3 completes two tasks at all five efforts, while
Kimi K3 has no task completed at all three efforts.</p>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A12" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix L </span>Automated Search for Task-Selection Methods</h2>

<div id="A12.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A12.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We investigate whether a coding agent can find task-selection methods
that better estimate a new model’s score on the full task set. The agent
develops these methods using results from six models; we evaluate them
on a seventh model whose results are withheld throughout the search.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A12.F18" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2609.40284v1/appendix_autoresearch.svg" id="A12.F18.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/189;" width="548" height="189"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 18: </span><span id="A12.F18.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Validation gains do not generalize to the held-out model.</span>
Across 34 candidate methods, the coding agent receives only validation
errors. We measure test error separately on the held-out model. Each method selects 32
tasks. Error averages the mean absolute errors in partial score and
exact completion, in percentage points.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="A12.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">L.1 </span>Search and Evaluation</h3>

<div id="A12.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A12.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We provide the coding agent with results from six models on 107 OSWorld2
tasks. It can modify both how the tasks are selected and how scores on
the selected tasks are used to predict the full-set score. Each candidate
method selects exactly 32 tasks. We evaluate it using six-fold
leave-one-agent-out validation: five models are used to fit the method,
and the sixth to measure prediction error. The agent receives only this
validation error and can revise its method. We separately test each
candidate on the seventh model after fitting to all six available models.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A12.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">L.2 </span>Validation Gains Do Not Generalize to the Held-Out Model</h3>

<div id="A12.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A12.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A12.F18" title="Figure 18 ‣ Appendix L Automated Search for Task-Selection Methods ‣ cua-speedrun: Standardized Benchmarking of the Speed of Computer-Use Agents" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a> compares validation and test error across
34 candidate methods. Validation error falls from 2.43 to 0.01 percentage
points, while error on the held-out model changes from 3.90 to 4.00
percentage points. The search nearly eliminates validation error without
improving the estimate for the new model. Validation errors guide repeated
method selection, allowing the search to overfit these six models.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</article>
</div>
